_note: Questionnaires and the survey. Wording was entered from the team's questionnaire document and still needs verification against the official versions (wordingVerified:false). Thresholds (bands) come from the same document and need counsellor approval (approved:false). descriptive:true means a descriptive grouping, not a clinical cut-off. 'offer' says when a scale is suggested: feelings and plate keys. placement.survey and placement.scales choose where they appear in the journey: 'pathwayEnd' or 'off'. Change them once the journey map is final.

scales.name: PHQ-4
scales.stem: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

items.q: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless

scales.name: WHO-5 Well-Being Index
scales.stem: Please indicate which option best describes how you have been feeling over the last two weeks.
o: Less than half of the time
More than half of the time

bands.label: Below the commonly used well-being threshold

items.q: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits.
I have felt calm and relaxed.
I have felt active and vigorous.
I woke up feeling fresh and rested.
My daily life has been filled with things that interest me.

scales.name: PSS-4 Perceived Stress Scale
scales.stem: The questions ask about your feelings and thoughts during the last month. For each question, select how often you felt or thought a certain way.
scales.dir: Higher scores mean more perceived stress. There are no validated severity bands, so none are shown.

items.q: In the last month, how often have you felt that you were unable to control the important things in your life?
In the last month, how often have you felt confident about your ability to handle your personal problems?
In the last month, how often have you felt that things were going your way?
In the last month, how often have you felt difficulties were piling up so high that you could not overcome them?

scales.permissionNote: Check reproduction permission before wider use.

scales.name: Insomnia Severity Index
scales.permissionNote: Disabled: items must not be reproduced until the rights holder confirms permission.

scales.name: UCLA 3-Item Loneliness Scale
scales.stem: How often do you feel the following?
scales.dir: Higher scores mean more reported loneliness.

items.q: How often do you feel that you lack companionship?
How often do you feel left out?
How often do you feel isolated from others?

scales.name: Oslo Social Support Scale (OSSS-3)
scales.dir: Higher scores mean more perceived support.

items.q: How many people are so close to you that you can count on them if you have great personal problems?
How much interest and concern do people show in what you do?
o: A lot of interest and concern

items.q: How easy is it to get practical help from neighbours if you should need it?

scales.name: Brief Resilience Scale
scales.stem: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each statement.
scales.dir: Higher scores mean an easier recovery from stress.

items.q: I tend to bounce back quickly after hard times.
I have a hard time making it through stressful events.
It does not take me long to recover from a stressful event.
It is hard for me to snap back when something bad happens.
I usually come through difficult times with little trouble.
I tend to take a long time to get over setbacks in my life.

scales.name: Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale
scales.stem: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each statement.

items.q: On the whole, I am satisfied with myself.
At times, I think I am no good at all.
I feel that I have a number of good qualities.
I am able to do things as well as most other people.
I feel I do not have much to be proud of.
I certainly feel useless at times.
I feel that I am a person of worth, at least on an equal plane with others.
I wish I could have more respect for myself.
All in all, I am inclined to feel that I am a failure.
I take a positive attitude toward myself.

survey.name: Understanding your experience
survey.stem: There are no right or wrong answers. Choose the options that best describe your experience.

items.q: How intense would you say this problem has been for you?
How frequently have you been experiencing this concern?
How long have you been experiencing this concern?
How much has this concern affected your everyday life? (For example your academics, sleep, relationships, concentration or daily routine.)
How difficult has it been for you to manage or cope with this concern?
o: Extremely difficult. I feel unable to manage it on my own

items.q: How has this concern changed over time?
o: It has remained about the same

items.q: A question about your safety. Have you recently had thoughts of hurting yourself, ending your life, or hurting someone else?
